findings.title: Primary actions that are not recording
findings.detail: Online booking (Website, Book appointment, status No recent conversions, All conv. 57.00, 9.4% of All conv. over the whole report (2026-10-14 to 2026-11-12)) is Primary, so bidding uses it, and its status is No recent conversions.

rules.label: Official
rules.rule: Awaiting conversions and No recent conversions mean no conversion was recorded in the last 7 days. Misconfigured means recording has stopped because of a setup error or a broken tag. Tag inactive means Google no longer sees the tag.
rules.source: Google Ads Help, Troubleshooting conversion tracking status

rules.label: Official
rules.rule: Bidding uses a conversion action only when it is Primary and in a goal the campaign uses. Secondary actions are reported in All conv. only, unless a custom goal includes them.
rules.source: Google Ads Help, About primary and secondary conversion actions

rules.label: Practitioner rule
rules.rule: When the conversion signal is broken, repairing tracking comes before any optimization.

checks.check: Trigger the conversion yourself on the live site and watch the tag. Tag Assistant does this: in Goals, Conversions, All conversions, hover over the Tracking status and choose Troubleshoot.
checks.label: Official
checks.source: Google Ads Help, Use Tag Assistant to troubleshoot your unverified or inactive conversion actions
checks.owner: Whoever manages Google Tag Manager or GA4

checks.check: Ask what changed on the website on or just before it stopped: a release, a new form or checkout, a new confirmation page address, or a tag manager publish.
checks.label: Practitioner rule

checks.check: Ask whether the booking or form tool changed on or just before it stopped: a new version, a new domain or a new confirmation page. A tool on another domain can lose the tag or the click identifier.
checks.label: Practitioner rule
checks.owner: Whoever owns the booking or form tool

checks.check: Check the consent banner. Default consent states must be set before any tag sends data, and updated after the visitor chooses. Check ad_user_data and ad_personalization, not only cookie storage.
checks.label: Official
checks.source: Google for Developers, Set up consent mode on websites

checks.check: Confirm the click identifiers still reach the site and the tag: gclid, gbraid or wbraid.
checks.label: Practitioner rule

checks.check: In Google Ads, open Goals, Conversions, All conversions and hover over the Tracking status of this action. Google shows its own diagnosis there.
checks.label: Official
checks.source: Google Ads Help, Troubleshooting conversion tracking status

checks.check: Read the change history for the days just before it stopped. Look for edits to conversion actions, to goals, and to the goals a campaign uses.
checks.label: Practitioner rule

findings.title: Two Primary actions in one category from different sources
findings.detail: In Submit lead form, 2 Primary actions come from 2 different sources: GA4 generate_lead (Google Analytics (GA4), Submit lead form, status Recording conversions, All conv. 182.00, 29.9% of All conv. over the whole report (2026-10-14 to 2026-11-12)); Website lead form (Website, Submit lead form, status Recording conversions, All conv. 181.00, 29.8% of All conv. over the whole report (2026-10-14 to 2026-11-12)). GA4 generate_lead and Website lead form carry a value, so value can be counted twice too. **Official:** Non purchase actions that are Primary and carry a value can double count value. Google's fix is to switch them to Secondary or to remove their value. (Google Ads Help, Data discrepancies: Factors and troubleshooting.)

rules.label: Practitioner rule
rules.rule: Two Primary actions in one category from different sources can be the same event counted twice. Confirm what each one records before changing either.

rules.label: Official
rules.rule: Google sets conversion actions created from Google Analytics to Secondary to prevent counting the same event twice for bidding, and its fix for double counting is to switch the extra action to Secondary.
rules.source: Analytics Help, Create Google Ads conversions based on Google Analytics key events

rules.label: Official
rules.rule: Bidding uses a conversion action only when it is Primary and in a goal the campaign uses. Secondary actions are reported in All conv. only, unless a custom goal includes them.
rules.source: Google Ads Help, About primary and secondary conversion actions

checks.check: Find out what each action records. Make one real conversion and see which actions count it.
checks.label: Practitioner rule
checks.owner: Whoever manages Google Tag Manager or GA4

checks.check: Check whether a tag now fires twice: on a reloaded confirmation page, on two pages, or from two tags for the same action.
checks.label: Practitioner rule
checks.owner: Whoever manages Google Tag Manager or GA4

checks.check: Check which goals each affected campaign uses, and whether a custom goal is in play. A report does not show this.
checks.label: Official
checks.source: Google Ads Help, About conversion goals

checks.check: Ask whether any campaign bids on value (Maximize conversion value or Target ROAS). If one does, a value counted twice is in what it bids on.
checks.label: Practitioner rule

findings.title: Lead actions counted as Every
findings.detail: Website lead form (Website, Submit lead form, status Recording conversions, All conv. 181.00, 29.8% of All conv. over the whole report (2026-10-14 to 2026-11-12)) is a Primary action counted as Every, so a second form or call from one click counts again.

rules.label: Official
rules.rule: Every counts each conversion after an ad interaction. One counts only one conversion per ad click. Google calls Every a good choice for sales, and gives leads as the case for One: only one unique lead per click.
rules.source: Google Ads Help, About conversion counting options

rules.label: Official
rules.rule: A change to the count setting applies to future conversions only.
rules.source: Google Ads Help, About conversion counting options

checks.check: Ask the business whether a second form or call from the same person is a second lead.
checks.label: Practitioner rule

findings.title: Categories with only Secondary actions
findings.detail: Get directions has only Secondary actions: Directions clicks (Website, Get directions, status Recording conversions, All conv. 62.00, 10.2% of All conv. over the whole report (2026-10-14 to 2026-11-12)). Bidding does not use them unless a custom goal includes them.

rules.label: Official
rules.rule: Bidding uses a conversion action only when it is Primary and in a goal the campaign uses. Secondary actions are reported in All conv. only, unless a custom goal includes them.
rules.source: Google Ads Help, About primary and secondary conversion actions

checks.check: Ask the business whether this is an outcome it would pay for.
checks.label: Practitioner rule

checks.check: Check which goals each affected campaign uses, and whether a custom goal is in play. A report does not show this.
checks.label: Official
checks.source: Google Ads Help, About conversion goals
